body:
Global crypto markets closed out August on a soft note, with total market cap sitting at $2.66T after a -2.60% decline in the past 24 hours and aggregate volume coming in at $84.3B. Fear and Greed printed 62 today versus 69 yesterday, a meaningful one-day compression that tells you sentiment is leaning cautious even if it hasn't tipped into neutral territory. BTC dominance at 59.2% and ETH dominance at 11.2% confirm the familiar pattern: when the market sells off, capital consolidates into bitcoin and the altcoin long tail bleeds harder. The mood is not panic, but it is not conviction buying either — end-of-month positioning, thin summer liquidity, and a news cycle that is simultaneously bullish on institutional flows and bearish on retail participation created a choppy, directionless session.

Bitcoin held the most ground of any major, trading at $78,522 with a 24h decline of just -0.30% and a 7-day loss of -1.60%. Volume was substantial at $28.88B, which suggests the dip is being absorbed rather than accelerated. The flat 1-hour print of 0.00% tells you BTC is digesting rather than trending into the close. The institutional bid is real and visible: Strategy returned to the market last week adding $370M in BTC in its first corporate purchase since June, and Metaplanet moved 4,800 BTC worth $377M to Coinbase — a custody transfer worth watching for any sign it precedes selling pressure. The $78,522 level is now a critical short-term anchor; a clean hold opens the path toward $80,000 as a psychological magnet, while a break below $77,000 would likely trigger a flush toward the mid-$74,000 range that has served as prior support.

Ethereum at $2,466.26 underperformed bitcoin slightly on a 24-hour basis at -0.38%, and the 7-day loss of -2.80% is twice as steep as BTC's. The more interesting divergence lives in the altcoin cohort. UNI is the standout on both sides of the ledger — it is the only major in positive territory over 24 hours at +0.49%, and its 7-day gain of +14.20% is the kind of move that warrants a catalyst check. Nothing in the data block explains it definitively, but the broader DeFi narrative around on-chain volume is getting a boost from Robinhood Chain beating Ethereum in daily revenue as memecoin trading dominates activity, which may be lifting governance tokens adjacent to that story. On the other end, ADA collapsed -3.71% on the day and -14.10% over 7 days — one of the worst drawdowns in the tracked universe with volume at just $0.38B, meaning the move is happening on thin participation, which makes it more fragile not less. XRP at $1.38 is down -10.10% over 7 days, and SOL at $103.51 is the sole mid-cap showing genuine weekly strength at +6.40% despite a -3.00% day, suggesting profit-taking on a relative winner rather than structural selling.

On the macro side, the regulatory picture is splitting in two directions simultaneously. Ireland has barred crypto from new tax-advantaged investment accounts, a retail-restrictive move that signals European regulators are not done tightening access even as institutions push forward. Countering that, NYSE owner ICE tapping tZERO for tokenized securities and taking a stake in the firm is a significant institutional infrastructure signal — this is legacy finance embedding itself in blockchain rails, not experimenting at the margins. Japan's regulator requesting a tax filing exemption for trust-type stablecoins in the 2027 reform cycle is incrementally constructive for the Asian market. The Bitmine ether purchase flagged by Tom Lee as part of crypto's strong Q3 performance, and Hyperliquid plus Pump.fun accounting for nearly 90% of a record $638M in crypto buybacks according to the FT, both point to on-chain capital formation that is quietly outpacing the headline price action.

Into September, the key catalysts are layered. Strategy's re-entry into BTC buying breaks a weeks-long silence and could encourage other corporate treasury desks to follow; watch for any additional corporate purchase announcements in the first week of the month. The Metaplanet Coinbase transfer needs resolution — if those coins stay custodied it is neutral to bullish, if they start moving to exchange wallets the market will notice fast. A sustained hold of $78,000 in BTC with UNI's DeFi momentum broadening into other protocol tokens would be a constructive signal that August's weakness was rotation rather than distribution. The risks are the mirror: a miss on any US macro print that resets rate-cut expectations, further European retail access restrictions gaining momentum, or thin September liquidity amplifying any forced selling from the ADA and XRP drawdowns into genuine capitulation. Watch the Fear and Greed number daily — another 5 to 7 point drop from today's 62 would shift the tactical posture from neutral to defensive.
